flawed_step: Step 4: the claim that each odd component of G−S sends at least 3 edges to S. Without the bridgeless hypothesis, a component can be joined to S by a single edge (a bridge), so this step fails.
counterexample: Gadget: take K4 on {a,b,c,d}, remove edge ab, and add a new vertex w adjacent to a and b. This gives 5 vertices; w has degree 2 and every other vertex has degree 3. Take three copies of the gadget and a central vertex v joined to the w of each copy. The result is a connected, simple, 3-regular graph on 16 vertices. Removing v leaves 3 components of odd size (5 each). Any perfect matching would need each of these odd components to have a vertex matched to v, but v can be matched to only one vertex. So the graph has no perfect matching.
assessment_summary:
Attempted proof (following Petersen's argument through Tutte's theorem):
1. Let G be a connected 3-regular graph on n vertices. Since 3n = 2|E|, n is even. — Justified (handshake lemma).
2. By Tutte's theorem, G has a perfect matching if and only if o(G−S) ≤ |S| for every S ⊆ V, where o counts odd components. — Justified (standard theorem).
3. Fix S. For each odd component C of G−S, the sum of degrees over C is 3|C|, which is odd. Edges inside C contribute an even amount to that sum, so the number of edges from C to S is odd. — Justified.
4. So each odd component sends at least 3 edges to S. — NOT justified. The previous step only gives an odd number, so at least 1. Getting 3 requires ruling out a single edge, which would be a bridge, and that is exactly the bridgeless hypothesis being dropped. This step fails.
5. Counting edges into S: 3·o(G−S) ≤ (edges from S) ≤ 3|S|, so o(G−S) ≤ |S|. — Does not follow, since it depends on step 4. With only step 3, the bound is o(G−S) ≤ 3|S|, which is too weak.
6. Tutte's condition holds, so G has a perfect matching. — Not justified (depends on step 5).

The failure is real, and the statement is false. Counterexample: three copies of a 5-vertex gadget (K4 with one edge subdivided by a vertex w), each w joined to a central vertex v. This gives a connected, simple, cubic graph on 16 vertices. For S={v}, o(G−S)=3 > 1, which violates Tutte's condition. Directly: each odd 5-vertex component needs a vertex matched outside itself, and the only option is v, which can cover just one. So there is no perfect matching, and the bridgeless hypothesis cannot be dropped.
